Maximum Concept Discrepancy drift detector (MCD-DD)

Source: R/dfr_mcd.R
dfr_mcd.Rd

Unsupervised online drift detector of Wan, Liang and Yoon (2024). A sliding window of window_size observations is split into n_sub sub-windows. Sets of m points sampled from a sub-window are embedded by a small neural network as the mean of the point encodings (the concept representation), and the maximum concept discrepancy (MCD) between two sub-windows is the distance between their representations. Every time a new sub-window arrives, its MCD to the previous sub-window is compared with a threshold; then the encoder is trained on the window by contrastive learning: sets from the same sub-window are pulled together, and sets with noise added (weak negatives, same sub-window; strong negatives, first and last sub-windows) pushed apart. The threshold is the percentile quantile of the MCD between sets of the same sub-window. Since it monitors the distribution of the observed features, it is used for virtual concept drift.

Usage

dfr_mcd(
  target_feat = NULL,
  window_size = 3000,
  n_sub = 10,
  m = 30,
  k = 10,
  hidden_size = 100,
  output_size = 100,
  eps_small = 1,
  eps_big = 10,
  learning_rate = 0.005,
  epochs = 1,
  temperature = 0.1,
  lambda = 1,
  percentile = 0.95,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

target_feat

Names of the columns to be monitored. NULL (the default) monitors every numeric column.

window_size

Size of the sliding window (a multiple of n_sub).

n_sub

Number of sub-windows in a window; the window slides by one sub-window (window_size / n_sub observations).

m

Number of points in a sample set.

k

Number of sample sets drawn from a sub-window (even).

hidden_size, output_size

Sizes of the hidden and output layers of the encoder.

eps_small, eps_big

Standard deviations of the Gaussian noise of the weak and strong negative sets.

learning_rate

Learning rate of the Adam optimiser.

epochs

Optimisation steps per window.

temperature

Temperature of the InfoNCE-like loss.

lambda

Weight of the gradient penalty that keeps the encoder close to 1-Lipschitz.

percentile

Quantile of the within-sub-window MCD used as threshold.

seed

Seed of the private random stream (initial weights, sampling and noise). NULL draws one from the session.

Value

dfr_mcd object. After fit(), drifter_output holds, on the last observation of every tested sub-window, its MCD to the previous sub-window (mcd) and the threshold (threshold); obj$distances has one row per tested sub-window with its MCD to each earlier sub-window of the window (the heatmaps of the paper).

Details

The detector follows the reference code (https://github.com/LiangYiAnita/mcd-dd, mcd.py, encoder.py and main.py), which differs from the paper in some points:

  • The encoder is Linear - ReLU - Linear - Sigmoid.

  • Sample sets are drawn with replacement. The positive term of a sub-window is the mean MCD over all pairs of its k sets.

  • The weak negative term compares the first k / 2 sets with the other k / 2 plus noise, and the strong one the sets of the first sub-window with those of the last one plus noise. Each is the mean MCD over the pairs of different indices.

  • The loss is log(sum(exp(pos / T)) / (sum(exp(pos / T)) + sum(exp(neg / T)))) plus lambda times the gradient penalty.

  • The gradient penalty is computed on the sets of the last sub-window. The norm of the input gradient of the summed encodings is taken over the points of a set, for every set and feature, as in the reference.

  • The MCD of two sub-windows in the test is the mean distance between the representations of their k sets, over pairs of different indices.

  • The first window only trains. From then on every window is tested with the encoder and threshold of the previous one, and then trained.

The data are not scaled, as in the reference; the noise levels refer to the units of the data. The network, its gradients (including the second derivatives of the gradient penalty) and Adam are written in R.

References

Wan, K., Liang, Y. and Yoon, S. (2024). Online drift detection with maximum concept discrepancy. Proceedings of the 30th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining, 2924-2935. doi:10.1145/3637528.3672016

See also

dfr_mcdd() is a different detector (mean comparison).

Examples

# \donttest{
library(daltoolbox)
library(heimdall)
# Mixture of two Gaussians whose weight changes at row 4001.
set.seed(1)
mixture <- function(n, p) {
  wide <- stats::runif(n) > p
  matrix(stats::rnorm(n * 3, 20, ifelse(wide, 50, 10)), n)
}
stream <- as.data.frame(rbind(mixture(4000, 0.2), mixture(2000, 0.8)))
detector <- dfr_mcd(window_size = 1000, m = 30, seed = 1)
model <- fit(detector, stream)
output <- model$drifter_output
which(output$mcd > output$threshold)
#> [1] 4100
# }
